summary: Defines StrEnum constants for storage. CONST_STORAGE_PROVIDER_TYPE enumerates provider identifiers (local, s3, s3express, azure_blob, azure_files, gcs, sftp, ftp, smb, nfs, minio, ssh, b2, github, r2, http) and is the key used by the backend registry, scheme table, profiles and facade. A _FindMemberMixin adds a case-insensitive find_member() lookup to the provider and access-type enums. Several further enums (access type, encryption type, connection status, transfer mode, compression type) are defined but not referenced elsewhere in src or tests.
key_classes: CONST_STORAGE_PROVIDER_TYPE — StrEnum of storage provider identifiers; the dispatch key for registry, schemes, profiles and facade
CONST_STORAGE_ACCESS_TYPE — StrEnum of access levels (read_only, write_only, read_write, admin); currently unused
CONST_STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_TYPE — StrEnum of encryption kinds; currently unused
CONST_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STATUS — StrEnum of connection states; currently unused
CONST_STORAGE_TRANSFER_MODE — StrEnum of binary/text/auto; currently unused
CONST_STORAGE_COMPRESSION_TYPE — StrEnum of compression kinds; currently unused
key_functions: _FindMemberMixin.find_member(v) -> Self | None — exact value lookup, then case-insensitive match on values; None for no match or None input
extension_points: Adding a provider means adding a CONST_STORAGE_PROVIDER_TYPE member, then wiring it through _schemes.SCHEMES, a storage profile spec, and (optionally) a registered backend
lifecycle_notes: Stdlib-only; imported eagerly by the package root and by _schemes/location, so it must stay dependency-free
documentation_hooks: Provider identifier reference table (enum value, schemes that map to it, profile class, backend status)
Maintainer checklist: adding a new provider
examples: examples/path_dispatch/example.py — prints detect_provider_from_path(...).value, i.e. CONST_STORAGE_PROVIDER_TYPE values
risks: NFS and SSH are provider members; NFS has no scheme in _schemes.SCHEMES and no profile, so it is a declared provider with no route to it
Five secondary enums are dead code (no references in src or tests outside this file), which can mislead readers into thinking encryption/compression/status are modelled here
find_member swallows all exceptions from str(v) and returns None, hiding bad inputs
open_questions: Should the unused enums (CONST_STORAGE_ACCESS_TYPE, CONST_STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_TYPE, CONST_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STATUS, CONST_STORAGE_TRANSFER_MODE, CONST_STORAGE_COMPRESSION_TYPE) be removed or wired up?
Is the NFS provider member intentional backlog, given it has no scheme or profile?

evidence.detail: CONST_STORAGE_PROVIDER_TYPE is eagerly imported and listed in root __all__
SCHEMES maps URL schemes to CONST_STORAGE_PROVIDER_TYPE members
tests StrEnum base, required members, lowercase values, and removal of legacy enums
only two commits (ca981bd reorganisation, 8ae8bb1 typing) -> stable
